args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After deploying v2.3.1 to production (us-east, us-west, eu-west), checkout-api failed health checks with an 18% error rate. (Its staging release candidate, v2.3.1-rc, was also marked unhealthy.) Rolled back all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, the service is healthy in all regions with a 0.2% error rate. Next steps: find the root cause in v2.3.1 before redeploying, and check why a release whose RC was unhealthy in staging was promoted.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened SEV2 incident INC-0001, which paged on-call.

- **Rollback:** The latest release, v2.3.1, was running in us-east, us-west and eu-west and failing health checks with an 18% error rate. v2.3.0 was the most recent release that was healthy in production. All three regions now run v2.3.0, and the error rate has dropped to 0.2%.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 says v2.3.1 was failing and that I rolled back to v2.3.0. It includes the error rates before and after.

**Still to do:** Someone needs to find what's wrong in v2.3.1 before it's deployed again. Its release candidate, v2.3.1-rc, was also marked unhealthy in staging, so it's worth finding out why it was promoted to production anyway. The incident lists both as next steps.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
